comment: Greetings Darin and City Council, I am writing to you as i am beyond frustrated with homeless and vagrant situation at Liberty Park. My wife and i use the park daily to walk and run our dogs. We have seen the homeless tents moving around the park daily for a couple of years now. Along with the homeless tents there is a significant presence of people living in their cars in the parking area at the Youth City Educational Center. Really? Homeless and children co-mingling? That is a no brainer and should have been addressed long ago! On many occasions i have used the Salt Lake City mobile app to report the camps. I have called to report suspicious activity to the Liberty Park Non-Emergency phone number several times as well. Now last night i am told there was a shooting and i know there have been several other altercations this summer alone. When is this going to be addressed? When is this going to stop! I have also been told by authorities that the situation is out of their hands as the Mayor has instructed police to stand down. Is this true? I have empathy for the homeless but letting them congregate and make Liberty Park their home is not the answer. There are other resources for them. You the council and the Mayor need to make this a priority now! Police need to patrol and break up these camps. Police need to have a presence within the park day and night. We do need to protect the homeless, but we also need to protect the people who work at the park and those who use the park as it is meant to be enjoyed. Regards, Don Tower

Hello! I recently read the SLtrib article on the SLC Foothill Plan and it really upsets me that a negative article like this is being distributed to people around the valley. This article provides inaccurate opinions and misinformation regarding that is biased to trail users that don't seem to understand that SLC is growing faster than many other cities in the country and people move here for the outdoor experience. I would like to let the council know that I'm an avid trail user (hike and bike) and I've only heard positive feedback from others that are out on the trails. I think that biking and hiking should be separated as much as possible, as designed in the plan. As for geotechnical concerns, I'm a civil engineer and I biked along all the trails after the recent events and observed no significant signs of erosion on the new trails. However all the old trails were severely eroded. Construction for this plan should start again next month as it's resulted in less user conflicts and better user experience than before! Please keep the foothill plan moving forward! Sincerely, Ryan O'Mahony

Hello, My name is Ryan O'Mahony. Over the past two weeks, there have been reports of gunshots four times within a few blocks of myself. I constantly see illegal activity and I don't feel safe walking my dog around my house even during the middle of the day. I have recently been informed that there will be an overflow shelter a few blocks north of my house. How can this be?!! We've already sacked up with the other resource center and our neighborhood is one of the highest in crime rate in the city!! I'm so upset with the city that we keep getting false promises and they're doing nothing to help families and businesses in the neighborhood other than the burden of additional crime. PLEASE HELP THIS NEIGHBORHOOD WE ARE DROWNING!! Sincerely, Ryan O'Mahony
